name: an alternate-line ladder published under two market ids renders one row per rung (executed-result parity)
description: The line axis suppresses nothing: it WIDENS the market-row dedup key from (selection, game) to (selection, game, line). Seed the shape that broke -- ONE game carrying TWO FanDuel CLOSE GAME_ALT_PASSING_YARDS markets, the second a re-key of the first published two days later at moved prices. That is not synthetic: FanDuel re-keyed its markets twice in 2025, once as a new source_market_id namespace across 14 week-1 games and once as a new source_event_id for the same game in week 12, leaving 739 duplicated (pid, esbid, line) keys across its player alt markets, every one at a different price. A user reported it as Aaron Rodgers carrying 124.5 twice in week 1, at -850 and -1100. The rung DOMAIN is the union of both markets, so the two rungs only the older one carries and the one only the newer one carries each render; the two rungs BOTH carry render once, at the newer market's price, which is the dedup policy (newest observation wins, ties broken on source_market_id). Four rows, never six. With the dedup suppressed this fixture goes red as six rows, with 199.5 and 249.5 each appearing twice at disagreeing odds -- which is the exact production symptom. The oracle asserts (line, odds) PAIRS rather than the two columns independently, so a row cannot silently take its line from one market and its price from the other.
